The [[1988 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XV Olympic Winter Games, was a winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Calgary]], [[Canada]], from 13 to 28 February 1988. A total of 1,423 athletes representing 57 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) (+8 from [[1984 Winter Olympics medal table|1984 Olympics]]) participated in 46 events (+7 from 1984) from 10 different [[Olympic sports#Winter Sports|sports and disciplines]] (unchanged from 1984).<ref name="Calgary">{{cite web|title=Calgary 1988 Winter Olympics|url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Calgary-1988/|work=Olympic.org|publisher=International Olympic Committee|access-date=22 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091005010206/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Calgary-1988/|archive-date=5 October 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> Five new events were contested at these Games—men's and women's [[Super Giant Slalom skiing|Super G]] in [[Alpine skiing at the 1988 Winter Olympics|alpine skiing]], team events in [[Nordic combined at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Nordic combined]] and [[Ski jumping at the 1988 Winter Olympics|ski jumping]], and women's 5000&nbsp;metres in [[Speed skating at the 1988 Winter Olympics|speed skating]]<ref name="Calgary" />—and two events returned to the program—men's and women's [[Alpine skiing combined|combined]] in alpine skiing.<ref name="speed skating event">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Speed skating at the 1988 Calgary Winter Games|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1988/SSK/|access-date=22 July 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100803070916/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1988/SSK/| archive-date= 3 August 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref>

As in the [[1984 Winter Olympics]], 17 NOCs won at least one medal and 11 of them secured at least one gold medal. The [[Soviet Union at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] returned to the top of the gold medal count with 11, relegating [[East Germany at the 1988 Winter Olympics|East Germany]]—which took first place four years earlier—to second place with nine. The Soviet Union also collected the most overall medals (29), including the most bronzes (9). In a repeat of the [[1976 Summer Olympics]] in [[Montreal]] and mimicking [[Yugoslavia at the 1984 Winter Olympics|Yugoslavia]] at the 1984 Winter Games, [[Canada at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Canada]], as host nation, did not win any gold medal, totalling two silver and three bronze medals. Canadian hopes for a gold rested on the shoulders of [[Figure skating at the 1988 Winter Olympics|figure skater]] [[Brian Orser]], the reigning World champion and silver medalist at the Sarajevo Games.<ref>{{cite news|last=Orr|first=Frank|title=Orser cheerfully carries country's hopes|newspaper=[[Toronto Star]]|publisher=[[Daily News Brands|Star Media Group]]|date=14 February 1988|page=G.4}}</ref> A tight contest with [[Brian Boitano]] of the [[United States at the 1988 Winter Olympics|United States]] ended with the American taking the Olympic title.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brian Boitano: This Soldier's No Toy|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966825,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101126172922/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,966825,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2010|access-date=23 July 2010|newspaper=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=29 February 1988|author=Jill Smolowe|author2=Ellie McGrath}}</ref> Athletes from [[Norway at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Norway]] failed to win any event in Calgary, making this the first and so far only time that the country ended the Winter Olympics without a single gold medal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Despite Big '88 Losses, ABC Wants '92 Games|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=28 February 1988|author=Toronto Globe & Mail|page=6}}</ref> [[Italy at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Italy]]'s two gold medals were won by the same athlete: [[Alberto Tomba]], a first-time Olympian who was crowned Olympic champion in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1988 Winter Olympics|alpine skiing]]'s slalom and giant slalom events.<ref>{{cite news|last=Alfano|first=Peter|title=88 Winter Olympics; Tomba Captures 2d Gold|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/02/28/sports/88-winter-olympics-tomba-captures-2d-gold.html|access-date=23 July 2010|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=28 February 1988|location=New York|archive-date=25 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225080049/http://www.nytimes.com/1988/02/28/sports/88-winter-olympics-tomba-captures-2d-gold.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ski jumper [[Matti Nykänen]] of [[Finland at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Finland]] contributed to three of his nation's four gold medals by winning both individual events (first time by an Olympic ski jumper) and helping his team to win the collective title.<ref name="matti nykanen">{{cite web|title=Matti Nykänen |url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Athletes/All-Athletes/Athletes-NN-to-NZ/-Matti-NYKANEN-/ |work=Olympic.org |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=23 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100826040455/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Athletes/All-Athletes/Athletes-NN-to-NZ/-Matti-NYKANEN-/ |archive-date=26 August 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The performance of the [[Switzerland at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Swiss]] athletes ensured their nation's best result at the Winter Games, securing a record number of 15 medals, including a then-record of five gold medals that took 18 years to be improved.<ref name="SUI">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Switzerland|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SUI/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417092337/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SUI/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=23 July 2010}}</ref>

Five NOCs participated for the first time in the Winter Olympics—[[Fiji at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Fiji]], [[Guam at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Guam]], [[Guatemala at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Guatemala]], [[Jamaica at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Jamaica]], and [[Netherlands Antilles at the 1988 Winter Olympics|Netherlands Antilles]]<ref>{{cite news|last=Janofsky|first=Michael|title='88 Winter Olympics; Calgary Has It Down Cold|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/02/07/sports/88-winter-olympics-calgary-has-it-down-cold.html|access-date=23 July 2010|newspaper=The New York Times|date=7 February 1988|archive-date=23 May 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090523082928/http://www.nytimes.com/1988/02/07/sports/88-winter-olympics-calgary-has-it-down-cold.html|url-status=live}}</ref>—but none of them won a medal. Jamaica's lone entry, the [[Jamaica national bobsled team|Jamaican bobsled team]], inspired the making of the 1993 movie ''[[Cool Runnings]]''.<ref name="cool runings">{{cite news|last=Lamont|first=Tom|title=Frozen in Time: Jamaica's bobsled team, Calgary Winter Olympics, 13 Feb 1988|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/feb/07/jamaica-bobsled-calgary-olympics|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 February 2010|access-date=23 July 2010|archive-date=13 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213014733/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/feb/07/jamaica-bobsled-calgary-olympics|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Medal table==
{{See also|Olympic medal table}}
[[File:Alberto Tomba Zagreb 2009.jpg|thumb|Italian alpine skier [[Alberto Tomba]] won his country's two gold medals in his first Olympic participation.]]

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>
